Align text on center text (default is decimal)

Source: R/formatting.R
align_chr.Rd

align_chr() formats numbers and pads them on both sides of the decimal point (or another center character) so that every value has the same width. When the column is centered, the decimal points line up.

Usage

align_chr(
  x,
  accuracy = NULL,
  trim_leading_zeros = FALSE,
  drop0trailing = FALSE,
  add_plusses = FALSE,
  padding_character = NULL,
  center = ".",
  format_integers = FALSE,
  side = c("both", "left", "right"),
  NA_value = "",
  format_numeric_character = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

vector (numeric or character)

accuracy

number to round to. If NULL, the current default accuracy set with apa7_defaults() will be used.

trim_leading_zeros

if TRUE, leading zeros are removed (e.g., .45 instead of 0.45), as APA style requires for values that cannot exceed 1 (correlations, proportions, p-values). If FALSE (default), they are kept.

drop0trailing

Drop trailing zeros

add_plusses

if TRUE, positive numbers get a plus sign. If FALSE (default), they do not.

padding_character

character to use for padding, default is &numsp; (figure space). With the default, text is padded to equal rendered width in the default font family (see num_pad() and the width_aware_padding argument of apa7_defaults()).

center

text on which to align text. Center on decimal by default, but can be any text.

format_integers

If TRUE, integers will be formatted with digits

side

side on which to make text of equal width

NA_value

value to replace NA

format_numeric_character

format character variables with numeric content

...

additional arguments passed to signs::signs()

Value

character vector

Details

With a few minor details omitted, align_chr() does roughly this:

  1. If format_numeric_character = TRUE, converts text made only of digits, minus signs, and periods to numbers.

  2. Formats numbers with signs::signs(): rounds them to accuracy, replaces hyphens with true minus signs, and adds commas to large numbers. Plus signs are added if add_plusses = TRUE, leading zeros are removed if trim_leading_zeros = TRUE, and trailing zeros are dropped if drop0trailing = TRUE. Whole numbers are not given decimals unless format_integers = TRUE.

  3. Splits each value at the first center character, then pads the part before it on the left and the part after it on the right (side limits the padding to one side), so that every value has the same width on each side of the center.

By default, values are padded with figure spaces, which are as wide as a digit. With this default, if width_aware_padding = TRUE in apa7_defaults() (the default) and the default font is installed, values are instead padded to the same rendered width in that font (see num_pad()), so that values with minus signs, commas, or markdown still line up. Other padding_character values are counted in characters.

The padded values line up only if every cell in the column is aligned the same way. apa_flextable() centers the columns of numbers and lines up padded values (see its Details).

Examples

align_chr(c(1, 10, 100))
#> [1] "  1" " 10" "100"
